messages:
ashwin: Heads-up — over the last 48h we’ve seen a cluster of failures concentrated in rack-21 (server slots 3,4,7,8). Pattern looks like hard Xid events followed by degraded ECC counts and eventual device disconnect.

maria: Ugh. Same vendor batch as last month?

ashwin: Yeah, all four cards share serial prefix GVB2-22*. Suspect bad batch from vendor lot.

gpu-monitor-bot: Alert: gpu_xid_errors > 10 in 5m for rack=21 (hosts: r21-s03,r21-s04,r21-s07,r21-s08) :exclamation:

david: Can you paste a sample dmesg/ipmi? Also are we seeing PCIe errors?

ashwin: Pasted below — from r21-s07 after it soft-failed and lost the kernel device.

```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00:0): 79, GPU at PCI:0000:3b:00.0
[ 1234.567912] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568000] pcieport 0000:00:1c.7: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: id 00e0
[ 1234.568020] pcie 0000:3b:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Receiver ID
```

ashwin: Also saw elevated ECC corrected counts right before the Xid.

emily: Any BIOS/BMC firmware drift on those hosts? I've seen link flaps after BMC updates in other fleets.

maria: r21 hosts are on BMC 2.54, BIOS 1.3. No recent fleet-wide updates logged for that rack.

david: Running quick checks — try toggling peer-to-peer and gen3 enforcement temporarily on affected hosts to see if stability improves. Could be negotiation bug.

ashwin: Will try. Quick remediation plan I propose: 1) Drain affected hosts from scheduler, 2) Offboard VMs/containers, 3) Pull cards for sanity tests (stress & memtest), 4) RMA batch if cards fail, 5) Flag serial prefix in local quarantine.

maria: Agree. Also good to capture PCIe link logs (set pcie_aspm=off?) and full nvml traces. Add a packet capture on the host for any weird NVLink chatter?

emily: Can ops do an emergency capacity rebalancing? We’ll lose ~8 GPUs from capacity if we drain all four hosts. Which pools affected?

ashwin: It hits our dev and test pools mostly. Prod unaffected for now, but headroom for nightly jobs is tight.

vendor-ops: Thanks for the report — we’re opening a high-priority case. Can you attach serials and the nvfan and nvlink logs? We’ll push to engineering.

ashwin: Serial list: [GVB2-22011, GVB2-22012, GVB2-22018, GVB2-22019]. I’ll upload the logs to the support case.

david: Quick troubleshooting notes I ran on r21-s04:
```
# soft-reset GPU
echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:3b:00.0/reset
# check link
lspci -vvv -s 0000:3b:00.0 | grep -i "LnkSta"
```

david: Reset allowed the device to come back but it had recurring ECC spikes ~2 minutes later. Suggests hardware marginality, not transient config.

emily: We should treat this as a recurring-batch postmortem. Proposal: short RCA doc, vendor RMA, tag inventory, and add one-off alert to detect serial-prefix spikes so we can auto-quarantine.

maria: +1. Also suggest we add a gating rule in provisioning: reject cards from that serial prefix until vendor confirms fix. Might be annoying but prevents future rollouts.

ashwin: Short-term mitigations I’ll run this afternoon: 1) Drain r21-s03/04/07/08, 2) Add alert: if >2 GPUs with same serial prefix generate P1, 3) Disable peer-to-peer on those hosts. Long-term: request vendor run manufacturing trace + firmware update.

vendor-ops: We will prioritize manufacturing trace and check for lot-specific firmware patches. If confirmed, we can do cross-ship replacements under RMA and escalate to expedited shipping.

david: For the postmortem let's capture: timeline, full logs, stress-test results, serial batch analysis, cost impact (capacity lost + expedited RMAs), and action items (quarantine rule, provisioning gating, alerting).

emily: I’ll start a skeleton postmortem doc and link it here once ready. Can someone own the RMA coordination?

ashwin: I’ll own RMA and on-site pulls this week. david you okay owning the postmortem writeup?

david: Yep I’ll take the writeup.

maria: Let’s also check telemetry to see if similar serial prefixes exist in other regions — could be wider. I’ll run a quick query on inventory.

gpu-monitor-bot: Note: Added temporary alert rule: serial_prefix_quarantine for GVB2-22* (threshold 2 devices) :lock:

ashwin: Thanks — will update after the pulls. Plan to post initial RCA draft by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

emily: Great. Keep the channel updated for any vendor response or if we need to escalate to ops leadership.

vendor-ops: Received logs and serials. Case #VND-8123 opened. ETA preliminary analysis 24-36h.
